name: text-field
summary: A labelled text-entry pattern built on native `<input>` and `<select>` elements. Mirrors the [Web-ODS Shared Library → Text field](https://www.figma.com/design/0o8SL5BEk8wHtgud00dRyg/Web-ODS-Shared-Library?node-id=698-47055&m=dev) (`698:47055`) under the LifeLock mode pick. The native HTML intentionally diverges from the Figma div / instance tree — visual + token fidelity is the bar, not structural fidelity.

properties.name: type
properties.description: Drives the control structure. Mirrors the Figma `Type` property (`Default` → `text`, `Dropdown` → `select`, `Combined`, `Splited` → `split`).

properties.name: label
properties.description: Field title rendered as a `<label for>`. Omit for a label-less field (supply an `aria-label` upstream).

properties.name: helperText
properties.description: Instructional message below the control, wired via `aria-describedby`. Recolours to `--color-text-error` when `error` is set.

properties.name: value
properties.description: Initial value bound to the native input.

properties.name: required
properties.description: Appends a `*` marker to the field title.

properties.name: error
properties.description: Adds `is-error` + `aria-invalid="true"`, paints the critical border, recolours the helper.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Sets the native `disabled` attribute and paints the disabled trio.

properties.name: selectOptions
properties.description: Native `<option>` rows for the standalone select.

properties.name: prefixLabel
properties.description: `aria-label` for the prefix select in combined / split.

properties.name: id
properties.description: Code-only. Wires the control `id` + `<label for>` + `aria-describedby`. No Figma component-property counterpart — an accessibility id, not a designer-set value. Pass a unique value per page.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Bound to the native control `name` (form submission).

properties.name: prefixOptions[].value
properties.description: Consumer-set. Bound to the prefix `<option value>`.

properties.name: prefixOptions[].selected
properties.description: Consumer-set. Pre-selects the prefix row (`<option selected>`).

variants.values: `text` (native `<input type="text">`) / `password` (native `<input type="password">` + reveal button) / `select` (native `<select>`) / `combined` (prefix `<select>` + `<input>` in one bordered wrapper) / `split` (separate prefix box + input box).
`default` / `hover` / `focused` — pseudo-class driven (`:hover` / `:focus-visible` on the native control). No `[data-state]` freeze hook; the AllStyles gallery shows the prop-driven states instead.

accessibility: The field title is a real `<label for>` bound to the control `id`; the helper is referenced from the control via `aria-describedby`.
`error` sets `aria-invalid="true"` so assistive tech announces the invalid state; the helper carries the human-readable reason.
Focus ring uses `:focus-visible` so it only paints on keyboard navigation; pointer focus stays quiet.
The password reveal is a real `<button type="button">` with `aria-pressed` and a state-accurate `aria-label` ("Show password" / "Hide password").

The standalone `select` uses the **native UA arrow** in Firefox / Safari (no icon-partial child, which would require the experimental `<button>`-in-`<select>` markup that breaks the native control). Chromium 135+ styles the `::picker(select)` menu via `appearance: base-select`; every other browser keeps the fully-functional native popup.

WCAG: resting + focus borders meet AA non-text contrast against `--color-bg-input`; disabled paint retains a visible outline per WCAG 2.2 § 1.4.11. Per the Figma guidance frame (`984:2201`), inputs should sit on the primary background — avoid placing them on accent / status surfaces where the border contrast is not guaranteed.
